standard.title: Cartesian plane — 4 quadrants
standard.description: Locate points in the 4 quadrants of a Cartesian plane; describe changes to the coordinates when a point is moved to a different position in the plane
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can construct and use grid coordinate systems to describe position and movement in the first quadrant (AC9M5SP02). Students can locate integers on a number line (AC9M6N01). They have not yet extended the coordinate system to all four quadrants using negative integers.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can locate points in all 4 quadrants of a Cartesian plane and describe how coordinates change when a point is moved.
standard.notes: This standard closely parallels AC9M6N01 node 3 (integer coordinates). The two standards work together — N01 establishes the concept in a number strand context while SP02 develops it spatially. Avoid duplication of content; SP02 emphasises movement, transformation, and spatial description rather than integer meaning.

nodes.label: Extending coordinates to all four quadrants
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and name the four quadrants of the Cartesian plane and locate points with integer coordinates in all four quadrants.
nodes.minimum_width: Label the four quadrants of a Cartesian plane; plot at least eight points, two per quadrant; read the coordinates of plotted points in all quadrants.
nodes.typical_width: Plot and read coordinates in all four quadrants including on the axes; identify the quadrant from the signs of the coordinates (++, −+, −−, +−); describe the position of a point relative to the origin and the axes.
wider: Use the four-quadrant plane to map a local area, game board, or treasure hunt with reference point at origin
Connect four-quadrant coordinates to integer number lines: each axis is a number line — why does this mean four quadrants?

response_modes.reason: Students must learn to identify quadrants from coordinate sign patterns (++, −+, −−, +−) rather than re-counting from the origin each time. This sign-convention reasoning needs explicit scaffolding before students can describe coordinate changes that cross axes in Node 2.

nodes.hinge_reason: Reliable four-quadrant plotting and coordinate reading is the prerequisite for Node 2. Students who confuse coordinate signs or quadrant membership cannot describe coordinate changes for movements that cross axes.
success_criteria: Student correctly plots points in all four quadrants.
Student reads coordinates of points in all quadrants and correctly identifies the quadrant from coordinate signs.

nodes.label: Describing coordinate changes when moving a point
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe how the coordinates of a point change when it is translated horizontally, vertically, or diagonally in the Cartesian plane.
nodes.minimum_width: Move a point horizontally and describe the change to x-coordinate; move a point vertically and describe the change to y-coordinate; state which coordinate changes and by how much for each movement.
nodes.typical_width: Describe coordinate changes for horizontal, vertical, and diagonal movements including movements that cross axes (changing sign); predict the new coordinates of a point after a described movement; connect movements to positive/negative integer addition.
wider: Investigate systematic translations of shapes on the Cartesian plane — if every vertex moves +3 horizontally and −2 vertically, how do coordinates change?
Explore reflections across axes: if a point at (3, −4) is reflected across the x-axis, what are the new coordinates? Identify the sign pattern.

response_modes.reason: Students often confuse horizontal and vertical movements with x- and y-coordinate changes. The explicit reasoning chain — horizontal movement changes only x, vertical movement changes only y — prevents persistent confusion and provides a tool for checking transformations.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Coordinate movement connects to transformation geometry (translations and reflections), integer addition, and spatial reasoning. The reflection sign-pattern investigation is particularly accessible and revealing for advancing students.
success_criteria: Student correctly identifies which coordinate changes when a point is moved horizontally or vertically.
Student predicts the new coordinates of a point after a described movement.
